site.name: Michael Chariga
site.headline: Research, Evaluation & Data Systems Specialist
site.intro: Research, evaluation and data systems specialist based in Nairobi. I work with data to understand what is happening in programmes, identify what needs to improve, and generate evidence that supports better decisions and results.
site.about: I work with data to understand what is happening in programmes, identify what needs to improve, and generate evidence that supports better decisions and results. I am a research and evaluation specialist with five years of experience in monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) systems, participatory research and data-driven programme design across Kenya and Tanzania. I work across the whole cycle, from instruments and sampling to training field teams, building data quality systems and dashboards, and writing findings for non-technical readers. So far that work has been in education, agriculture and parenting programmes, and I am keen to apply the same methods to new questions and sectors.
site.sub: I work with data to understand what is happening in programmes, identify what needs to improve, and generate evidence that supports better decisions and results.
site.open_to: Open to roles, consultancy and collaborations

projects.title: Field Assessment Report: Improving Farmer Training on AE Practices
projects.desc: Endline evaluation of one-week agroecology training with 10 partner organisations across 42 sub-counties in western Kenya. 223 farmers and 63 practices assessed; 48 practices rose. Co-authored with Muchugia Susan for the Kenya Agroecology Hub, funded by the Conservation Food and Health Foundation.

projects.title: Tephrosia for Livestock Parasites: Farmer Practices
projects.desc: Six focus group discussions with 58 farmers across five Migori sub-counties (13 to 17 January 2025), following up the December 2024 farmer survey for the Rural Farmers Research Network. Farmers found tephrosia effective against livestock parasites, best used as prevention; ratio 1:5 worked best for most, while 1:3 was risky for young animals. Prepared by Michael Chariga.
projects.label: Read the report (PDF)

projects.title: Fermented Feeds Lab Results: CoP Presentation
projects.desc: Lab nutrient results for fermented poultry feeds from five organisations (CRANE, MHAC, RFRN, RODI, SOFDI), on a dry matter basis and checked against optimal ranges. Crude protein and digestible energy were low for most farmers; calcium and fibre need review in RFRN and SOFDI. Presented at the 2026 Kenya Agroecology Hub Community of Practice meeting, Kitale.
projects.label: View the slides (PDF)

projects.title: Student Learning and a Farmer Research Network
projects.desc: Six-month pilot (two school terms) with 171 fifth-grade pupils in Kurutiyange and Naora, Kuria West, testing whether pupils could help a farmer research network collect data while building practical, CBC-aligned skills. The hypothesis that pupils would collect better data than their parents was rejected, but the learning gains were clear. Co-authored with Tekviah Munandi, Esther Njeri and Evans Odhiambo.
projects.label: Read the report (PDF)

projects.title: Termite FRN KoboToolbox Pipeline
projects.desc: R pipeline that pulls multi-version KoboToolbox forms, flattens nested repeat groups into analysis-ready wide data, removes duplicates and exports stage-specific Excel workbooks for the 2025 Long Rain and Short Rain seasons.

Co-author of maths education papers and presenter at AFRICME7.

scope.foot: Travel, fieldwork and other project expenses are discussed as part of the scope.

packages.name: MEL framework starter
includes: Theory of change or results chain
packages.note: Best for small programmes. Complex multi-partner programmes are quoted separately.

packages.name: Digital survey system
includes: One KoboToolbox, ODK or SurveyCTO form
packages.note: Excludes survey licences, large-scale data collection, enumerator wages and field travel.

packages.name: Programme dashboard
includes: Up to two rounds of revisions
packages.note: Automated pipelines, multiple live sources, hosting and access controls are scoped separately.

packages.name: Data analysis and findings brief
includes: Cleaning and validation of one supplied dataset
packages.note: Advanced modelling, complex qualitative coding and very large datasets are quoted separately.

packages.name: MEL or data training
packages.note: Venue, travel, accommodation and catering are additional.

extras.name: Evaluation design package
extras.note: Covers the design only, not conducting the evaluation or collecting field data.

extras.name: Monthly MEL and data support
extras.note: Hours, response times and exclusions are set out in the agreement.

terms: Small projects: 50% on commencement and 50% on delivery.
Larger projects: payments tied to inception, draft deliverables and final approval.
Two reasonable revision rounds are included; extra changes outside the agreed scope are chargeable.
Invoicing currency, payment method and taxes are agreed before work starts.
